findings: Complete current MDX SHA-256 is 4f98b66f3894e35188822c8717780952df0cc38531265713ead922d4595190ed; all 6 declared sources passed current access review.

Claims remain bounded to adaptable family-meeting and communication practices from university extension sources, general inherited-property context from the USDA Forest Service, and current MRX inheritance and seller-control guidance. No source is converted into a private title, probate, authority, consent, value, tax, contract, or transaction conclusion.

The article invents no real owner, property, buyer, contract, transaction, price range, production, reserves, forecast, testimonial, success rate, or owner-specific legal, tax, accounting, title, appraisal, engineering, investment, or transaction conclusion.

sources_inspected.label: University of Minnesota Extension, Preparing to meet with your transition and estate planning team (reviewed 2023; accessed 2026-08-14)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: University of Minnesota Extension transition-planning guidance recommends preparing goals and questions in writing, involving affected parties, and using family meetings as part of a fact-based planning process.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article adapts only those meeting-preparation practices to a pre-assessment family conversation. It does not treat farm or estate guidance as mineral-rights law or use it to determine ownership, authority, consent, title, value, tax, or whether to sell.

sources_inspected.label: University of Minnesota Extension, Farm business transfer strategies (accessed 2026-08-14)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: University of Minnesota Extension farm-business transfer guidance recommends brief and specific communication that avoids accusation, insult, and blame and describes structured family-business meetings.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article adapts only those communication disciplines. It does not equate a mineral interest with a farm business or derive any legal, ownership, authority, consent, valuation, tax, or transaction conclusion from the source.

sources_inspected.label: Utah State University Extension, Estate Planning Toolkit: Starting the Estate Planning Conversation (accessed 2026-08-14)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The Utah State University Extension Estate Planning Toolkit recommends a calm setting, a clear intention, input from people directly affected, and an agenda that may span multiple conversations.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article adapts only those conversation practices. It does not treat the source as mineral-specific advice or use it to determine probate, title, ownership, authority, consent, value, tax, or disposition.

sources_inspected.label: USDA Forest Service, Heirs Property: Legal and Cultural Dimensions of Collective Landownership (accessed 2026-08-14)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The USDA Forest Service overview describes heirs property as inherited real property that can involve multiple heirs and fragmented collective ownership.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses it only as general background that family shorthand may conceal distinct interests and unresolved records. It does not apply heirs-property law to mineral ownership or determine any reader’s title, authority, consent, signature, probate, or sale rights.

sources_inspected.label: Mineral Rights Xchange, Mineral Rights Inheritance in Texas: What Heirs Need to Know Before Selling (accessed 2026-08-14)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The current MRX inherited-mineral-rights guide explains that inherited-interest review depends on the actual estate, deed, trust, operator, and title records and that family relationship alone does not settle ownership or sale authority.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses it only to separate a family conversation from professional ownership and authority review. It does not restate the inheritance workflow or decide title, acreage, probate, authority, signatures, value, tax, or whether to sell.

sources_inspected.label: Mineral Rights Xchange, Selling Mineral Rights: Selling Process For Mineral Owners (accessed 2026-08-14)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The current MRX seller-control guide explains that owners can gather information, request written terms, pause, seek independent advice, and decline to proceed through a possible sale process.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses it only to preserve owner agency when the family selects a later information-gathering step. It does not retell the selling sequence, compare offers, interpret documents, determine value, or recommend a sale.
